About

I’m Do Heon, a Brown University student pursuing separate degrees in computer science and music, graduating in May 2027.

My work spans AI systems for business research, financial reporting automation, and generative 3D research. I’m interested in making complex systems useful, reliable, and clear.

Career

A research lab, two years in a rehabilitation classroom, then AI work in Seoul.

  1. NowFall 2026

    Brown University

    Final year · Computer Science & Music · Providence

    Back at Brown.

    Back in Providence for my final year, taking Embedded Systems, Scientific Visualization and more.

    • Beginning a collaboration with a cognitive science group at Brown to build a tool that measures and visualizes human movement, which I hope to one day bring to physical education for students with disabilities.
  2. 2026Mar — Aug

    LG Business Research

    Full-time Research Assistant · AI Transformation · Seoul

    Finding the signal.

    At LG Group’s in-house consulting company, I proposed and led a project to automate weekly news selection around researchers’ own editorial priorities: a LangGraph pipeline with TF-IDF and Korean-language embeddings, exposed as an MCP server so researchers could query it directly in Claude.

    • Surfaced 19% of the topics researchers went on to publish across 11 weeks, with a 22% top-5 hit rate against the baseline’s 11%.
    • Designed source-specific retrieval for regulatory filings, executive changes and CEO statements; general-purpose LLM search missed roughly 25% of verified events.
    • Built a video-to-report pipeline (Parakeet transcription, pyannote diarization, LLM speaker naming) that turned about 200 conference talks into firm-wide reports.
    • Built a weekly scraper that collects book-related articles for researchers to draw on, with an LLM that works out each article’s author, its main book (one article can mention many) and its real publication date, since the date metadata is almost always wrong.
    • Helped with weekly trend sensing, using the research skills I built at KB.
    2.8×

    topic coverage vs. a prompted-Claude baseline

    • LangGraph
    • MCP
    • Retrieval
    • Evaluation

  4. 2025Aug 2025 — Feb 2026

    KB Securities

    Full-time Digital Transformation Intern · Global Client Distribution · Seoul

    A better morning brief.

    At South Korea’s sixth-largest brokerage, I automated the Executive Vice President’s morning news briefing: a Python and LangGraph pipeline with MiniLM deduplication, LLM relevance filtering and asset-class classification, kept nearly free by using open RSS feeds and pre-compressing text before the LLM.

    • Automated daily Excel reports covering 12,000+ ownership disclosures and treasury-stock filings across 2,600+ companies (OpenDART, KRX, Yahoo Finance).
    • Cut weekly report prep from 30 minutes to seconds by turning Bloomberg economic-calendar events into a formatted PowerPoint slide.
    • Interpreted for clients, and built a real-time, low-latency speech-to-text app on Naver CLOVA to support myself while translating.
    • Researched for the firm’s weekly and annual reports: pulling data from the Bloomberg Terminal, digging into sources, and building the visualizations and Excel models behind them.
    • Made the animated charts for KB Securities’ official LinkedIn posts.

  5. 2023Oct 2023 — Jul 2025

    Yonsei Rehabilitation School

    Full-time teacher’s assistant · Republic of Korea military service

    The work that shaped me most.

    For my mandatory service I worked full time with K–12 students with physical and developmental disabilities. Some days I sat beside a student working through a counting lesson on an iPad; other days I walked alongside students with brain lesions as they learned to use a wheelchair.

    Progress was slow and uneven, and I learned to notice the small signs of change. My most memorable moment was watching a student slowly realize that something he had thought impossible might be feasible after all. Since then, I’ve wanted to build things that change how students learn and what they believe is possible for themselves.

    • Kept my research with Brown Visual Computing Lab going remotely throughout.
  6. 2023May 2023 — May 2025

    Brown Visual Computing Lab

    Undergraduate Researcher · Providence

    Language into 3D worlds.

    I helped develop a 3D scene-generation method in which an LLM writes layout programs for any kind of object, with no training on 3D scene datasets. The work led to a co-first-author preprint and a SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 paper (see Research).

    • Reduced LLM hallucinations to 1.16 per 1,000 generated objects with backtracking, in-context learning and chain-of-thought prompting.
    • Built an automated LLM evaluator for scene quality and improved its agreement with human judgments by 19 percentage points.
    ~80%

    of user-study comparisons preferred over NVIDIA ATISS and DiffuScene

Research

LLMs for open-universe 3D scenes.

Citations92View on Google Scholar ↗
01
ACM SIGGRAPH Asia 2025Second authorCited by 11

Procedural Scene Programs for Open-Universe Scene Generation: LLM-Free Error Correction via Program Search

SummaryInstead of having an LLM write constraints for a solver, we let it place objects one by one in code, then repair collisions with an LLM-free search over the program. In perceptual studies, people preferred these layouts 82% and 94% of the time over two leading declarative methods.

Read the paper ↗Research code ↗
02
arXiv · 2025Second authorCited by 3

Imperative vs. Declarative Programming Paradigms for Open-Universe Scene Generation

SummaryThe preprint that framed the question: should an LLM describe a room as constraints for a solver, or as step-by-step placement code? It argues for code, adds an error-correction pass that edits the program directly, and proposes an automatic layout metric that tracks human judgment.

Read the paper ↗
03
arXiv · 2024Co-first authorCited by 78

Open-Universe Indoor Scene Generation using LLM Program Synthesis and Uncurated Object Databases

SummaryGenerates 3D rooms from any text prompt with no 3D training data: an LLM writes a layout program, an optimizer solves it, and a vision-language model finds matching furniture in huge, unlabeled mesh databases.

01 · Presentation

SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 talk

Presenting “Procedural Scene Programs for Open-Universe Scene Generation” on stage in December 2025: an LLM writes step-by-step programs that place each object in a 3D scene, and an LLM-free search repairs the layout.

02 · Graphics

Biome Begetters

Minecraft-style worlds generated in real time in C++ and OpenGL for Brown’s CS 1230: Voronoi cells become biomes, Simplex noise sets temperature, rainfall and height, and a procedural skybox cycles from day to night.

My part, in a team of four: the toon shading, which quantizes Phong lighting into flat bands, and the camera modes, an orbiting “beauty” view and a first-person walk that follows the terrain’s height.

  • C++
  • OpenGL
  • GLSL
GitHub ↗

03 · Guitar

Guitar Kontrol

A Max/MSP instrument for live guitar, performed on stage. My phone streams motion over OSC: tilting it bends the pitch, and hand gestures shape the EQ and a reverb’s size, decay and damping.

An FFT vocoder blends the guitar with a synth tone, a granular engine records and scatters it live, and a Jitter visual draws a polar rose from the pitch it hears.

  • Max/MSP
  • Jitter
  • OSC
